title: Fluent 2 home

title: Design getting started / official Figma kits
summary: Explains that Fluent 2 design assets are hosted as Figma UI kits whose properties map to the code libraries for handoff. Describes a tiered kit structure (design language, Core, Labs) and styling through Figma variables for color, stroke, radius, spacing, and size tokens.

title: Develop getting started
summary: Per-platform install and setup guidance for Fluent UI React v9 and the other Fluent platforms. For React it stresses React and TypeScript, Griffel CSS-in-JS styling, and wrapping the app in FluentProvider with a theme.
licenseNotes: Microsoft Fluent 2 documentation; summaries and links only, no assets retained

title: Layout
summary: Defines Fluent's layout system around proximity, a 4px-based spacing ramp, and grid anatomy of columns, gutters, margins, and regions. Covers breakpoint size classes and responsive techniques such as reposition, resize, reflow, show/hide, and re-architect.
licenseNotes: Microsoft Fluent 2 documentation; summaries and links only, no assets retained

title: Design tokens
summary: Explains Fluent's two-layer token model: context-agnostic global tokens holding raw values for color, typography, radius, stroke, and animation, and alias tokens that give those values semantic meaning. Notes built-in light, dark, high-contrast, and branded theming.
licenseNotes: Microsoft Fluent 2 documentation; summaries and links only, no assets retained

title: Color
summary: Documents three Fluent palettes: neutral grays for surfaces and text, shared semantic colors aligned across Microsoft apps, and per-product brand colors. Advises using semantic colors sparingly and pairing color with text or graphics for accessibility.
licenseNotes: Microsoft Fluent 2 documentation; summaries and links only, no assets retained

title: Typography
summary: Describes Segoe as Microsoft's signature typeface with native fallbacks per platform, and publishes per-platform type ramps giving name, weight, and size/line-height. Covers sentence-case writing, alignment, and contrast minimums.
licenseNotes: Microsoft Fluent 2 documentation; summaries and links only, no assets retained

title: Iconography
summary: Divides Fluent icons into system (MIT-licensed, regular and filled), product launch, and file type collections, with sizing and scaling guidance. Covers naming icons for the object they depict, filled modifiers, single-color constraints, and locale validation.
licenseNotes: Microsoft Fluent 2 documentation; summaries and links only, no assets retained

title: Elevation
summary: Explains elevation as perceived distance conveyed by shadow and light with a consistent light source. Documents a blur-indexed shadow ramp per light/dark theme with example use cases, and a luminosity adjustment for colored surfaces.
licenseNotes: Microsoft Fluent 2 documentation; summaries and links only, no assets retained

title: Motion
summary: States four motion principles (functional, natural, consistent, appealing) and advises matching duration to element size and distance while limiting linear easing. Covers common transitions, choreography via staggering, and no-motion and seizure-safety rules.
licenseNotes: Microsoft Fluent 2 documentation; summaries and links only, no assets retained

title: Accessibility
summary: Sets out accessibility expectations for Fluent experiences, noting components meet or exceed WCAG 2.1 AA. Covers logical headings, managed focus order, contrast ratios, reflow without horizontal scroll to a 320px breakpoint at 400% zoom, text zoom, alt text, plain language, and semantic code.
licenseNotes: Microsoft Fluent 2 documentation; summaries and links only, no assets retained

title: React component overview
summary: Discovery index for Fluent 2 Web that lists every core component with a one-line description and a link to its per-component usage page, and points to the React and Web Components storybooks.
licenseNotes: Microsoft Fluent 2 documentation; summaries and links only, no assets retained

title: field
summary: A field pairs a label with any data-entry control and can add info buttons, helper text, and validation states. Placeholder text must never carry essential information and must be paired with an accessible name, while disabled fields keep their label and helper text readable.
licenseNotes: Microsoft Fluent 2 documentation; summaries and links only, no assets retained

title: dialog
summary: Dialogs cover focused interactions: modal for blocking tasks, non-modal for helper flows, and alert only for potential loss. Titles are mandatory, focus must enter the container on open and return to the trigger on close, and dialogs should not be nested.
licenseNotes: Microsoft Fluent 2 documentation; summaries and links only, no assets retained

title: drawer
summary: A drawer is a secondary surface sliding in from a layout edge, available as an inline passive panel or an overlay panel that is modal by default. Keep flows to two or three steps, wrap body content in DrawerBody for scrolling, and confirm data-losing actions with a dialog.
licenseNotes: Microsoft Fluent 2 documentation; summaries and links only, no assets retained

title: accordion
summary: Accordions group related content into collapsible sections to lower cognitive load, with items closed by default and an option to allow several open together. Never hide information required for the current task inside one, and expose headers as buttons that set aria-expanded.
licenseNotes: Microsoft Fluent 2 documentation; summaries and links only, no assets retained

title: menu
summary: A menu is a hidden list of options opened from a trigger, suited to immediate actions or navigation rather than collecting input, for which select, dropdown, or combobox should be used. Checkbox and radio variants support settings, and submenu triggers need an accessible name.
licenseNotes: Microsoft Fluent 2 documentation; summaries and links only, no assets retained

title: nav
summary: Nav offers high-level wayfinding links to an app's main sections and supports only one level of category nesting, directing deeper hierarchies to Tree. Secondary actions must always be present in the DOM, and at narrow widths nav shifts from an inline drawer to an overlay drawer.
licenseNotes: Microsoft Fluent 2 documentation; summaries and links only, no assets retained

title: button
summary: Buttons trigger a single action and come in standard, split, menu, compound, and toggle variants, with links preferred for navigation. Limit a layout to one primary button, keep text and icon contrast sufficient, and supply accessible descriptions for disabled and split-button options.
licenseNotes: Microsoft Fluent 2 documentation; summaries and links only, no assets retained

title: tablist
summary: A tablist switches between closely related categories of content without leaving the page, defaulting to horizontal layout with an overflow menu when tabs cannot fit. Keep labels short and parallel, make the first tab active on first render, and label icon-only tabs accessibly.
licenseNotes: Microsoft Fluent 2 documentation; summaries and links only, no assets retained

title: toolbar
summary: A toolbar exposes frequently used actions for the current view and stays on one line, converting its last item into an overflow menu when space runs out. Group related actions with dividers, label the toolbar, and give icon-only buttons both tooltips and accessible names.
licenseNotes: Microsoft Fluent 2 documentation; summaries and links only, no assets retained

title: messagebar
summary: A message bar communicates product- or surface-level status in info, success, warning, and error variants, is always dismissible, and re-surfaces warnings and errors until resolved. Warning and error bars require an action and use assertive live regions, ordered most to least critical.
licenseNotes: Microsoft Fluent 2 documentation; summaries and links only, no assets retained

title: toast
summary: Toasts are temporary, non-critical status surfaces grouped as confirmation, progress, or communication, placed consistently in a corner and limited in number. Use timed dismissal when no action is needed and the intent property so icons and live regions match the message.
licenseNotes: Microsoft Fluent 2 documentation; summaries and links only, no assets retained

title: card
summary: A card is a flexible container for the information and actions tied to a single object, composed from optional preview, header, and footer slots in vertical or horizontal layouts. Control focus behavior with the focusMode property and label selectable cards accessibly.
licenseNotes: Microsoft Fluent 2 documentation; summaries and links only, no assets retained

title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
summary: WCAG 2.2 is a W3C Recommendation giving testable success criteria under Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, and Robust at levels A, AA, and AAA. title: DataGrid usage and API (v9 docs and package source)
summary: The v9 DataGrid documentation and source: declarative column definitions in which sorting requires a compare function; controlled or uncontrolled sort and selection state; a composite focus model with a per-cell focusMode; preview column resizing with sizing options; selection cells that need accessible names; and virtualization through a community extension that requires a memoized row renderer. No first-party Fluent 2 usage page exists for DataGrid or Table (both return 404), so this source is the authoritative evidence.
